title: Ted Sanders (@sandersted)

title: Ted Sanders (@sandersted)
summary:
Productive technologies make expensive things cheap.
What does GPT-4 make cheap?
Customization to a context.
This is why the use case I'm most excited by is tutoring/teaching. Lectures and textbooks and search results can't be tailored to an individual.
A conversation can be.

title: Ted Sanders (@sandersted)
summary:
Progress in software feels faster than progress in robotics.

Why? Is it outsourcing? Is it services being more difficult to automate? Is it non-robotic automation like shipping containers?
I wonder, genuinely.
Quoting @DKThomp
This is the chart that has launched a thousand takes.
The conclusion seems obvious: Everything the govt touches goes to infinity in price. Everything pure capitalism touches goes to zero.

title: Ted Sanders (@sandersted)
clean_title: The third wave of American philanthropy and its scale
summary:
New blog post: The third wave of American philanthropy
Hundreds of billions of dollars in new philanthropic capital will soon become liquid. The OpenAI Foundation holds 26% of OpenAI, worth about $220B at today’s valuation. Anthropic’s seven co-founders have pledged to give away 80% of their wealth and have instituted the most aggressive donor matching program for employees in tech history.
How much does this all add up to? And how meaningful is that in the context of philanthropy today?
I was doing some simple napkin math to wrap my head around the scale of what’s coming, and radicalized myself in the process. I had dramatically underappreciated the scale of the philanthropic capital that’s about to become available and the corresponding gap in talent and organizations that will be needed to make the most of it.
This piece aims to directionally sketch the scale of what’s coming, the gap in operational capacity needed to absorb it, and what we can do to fill it.
(Link to full post in reply)
clean_summary:
A new blog post discusses the upcoming surge of liquid philanthropic capital in the United States. The OpenAI Foundation holds 26% of OpenAI, valued at about $220 billion, and Anthropic’s co-founders have pledged to give away 80% of their wealth, with a strong donor matching program for employees.

The post estimates that this influx of capital is much larger than previously appreciated and highlights the significant gap in talent and organizations needed to effectively utilize it. It sketches the scale of the coming change, the operational capacity gap, and suggests ways to address it.
